title: Annular lower-integral bounds survive the shrinking gap
statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, mu a measure on R^(n+l), g : R^(n+l) -> [0, infinity] an arbitrary function, y in R^(n+l), (eps_k) and (c_k) real sequences, and s, r, L real numbers with s > 0. Assume eps_k -> 0 and c_k -> L. Assume also that, for all sufficiently large k, the lower Lebesgue integral of g over closedBall y r minus ball y ((1 + eps_k) s) is at most ofReal(c_k). Then the lower Lebesgue integral of g over closedBall y r minus closedBall y s is at most ofReal(L).
lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) (g : Amb n ℓ → ℝ≥0∞) (y : Amb n ℓ) (ε c : ℕ → ℝ) (s r L : ℝ), 0 < s → Tendsto ε atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto c atTop (𝓝 L) → (∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∫⁻ x in closedBall y r \ ball y ((1 + ε k) * s), g x ∂μ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c k)) → ∫⁻ x in closedBall y r \ closedBall y s, g x ∂μ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal L
